findings.title: website_name is not registered as an untrusted attribute, leaking TL0 users' website info to anonymous visitors
findings.body: The serializer lists `website` in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which suppresses it when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list, so for those same users the API still serializes `website_name`, which now includes not just the host but the full URL path (e.g. `example.com/private-page`). This defeats the purpose of hiding `website` for untrusted profiles and leaks information the site explicitly intends to hide. `website_name` must be added to `untrusted_attributes` alongside `website`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark, so the include guard is never called by AMS
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only invokes the conditional-include hook named `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark) — every other guard in this file follows that convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_card_image_badge?`). The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is dead code: the serializer never calls it. Consequently, when a user has no website, the JSON still contains `"website_name": null` instead of omitting the key, and the intended `website.present?` guard has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Untrusted-attributes spec list was not updated to cover website_name
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still contains only `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. Since this PR adds a new attribute derived directly from `website`, `:website_name` should be added to that list so the spec verifies it is suppressed for restricted users. As written, the existing test suite would not catch the leak of `website_name` (host plus full path) for TL0 profiles viewed anonymously — adding it would make the spec fail today and force the fix.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) is re-parsed up to three times per serialization
findings.body: The `website_name` method calls `URI(website.to_s)` once for the host (line 138) and again for the path (lines 143, 146, 149), meaning the URL string is parsed up to three times for every user serialized. This runs for every user in any payload using UserSerializer (user pages, staff lists, etc.). Parse the URI once into a local variable and reuse it for both `host` and `path`.

findings.title: Query string and fragment are silently dropped from the displayed path
findings.body: `website_name` builds the display string as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, discarding the query string and fragment. A user whose website is `http://example.com/profile?user=42` on a same-domain instance will see `example.com/profile` in their profile, which links correctly (the href uses the full `website`) but displays a URL that does not correspond to the link target. If showing the complete URL is the goal, the query/fragment should be preserved (or this limitation acknowledged).
